Globally Harmonized System of Classifica.subSubject: Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals

Globally Harmonized System of Classifica.subject: General Science

Globally Harmonized System of Classifica.fact: First widespread implementation set by OSHA was on March 26, 2012, requiring manufacturers to adopt the standard by June 1, 2015, and product distributors to adopt the standard by December 1, 2015.

Globuloviridae.subject: General Science
Globuloviridae.question: Crenarchaea of the genera _____ and Thermoproteus (both in Thermoproteaceae) serve as natural hosts
Globuloviridae.fact: Crenarchaea of the genera Pyrobaculum and Thermoproteus (both in Thermoproteaceae) serve as natural hosts.

Globuloviridae.subject: General Science
Globuloviridae.question: Pyrobaculum and _____ archaea serve as the natural host
Globuloviridae.fact: Crenarchaea of the genera Pyrobaculum and Thermoproteus (both in Thermoproteaceae) serve as natural hosts.

Globuloviridae.subject: General Science
Globuloviridae.question: There are four species in this family, assigned to a single genus, _____
Globuloviridae.fact: There are four species in this family, assigned to a single genus, Alphaglobulovirus.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: The _____ was Term for several kidney diseases.
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Glomerulonephritis (GN) is a term used to refer to several kidney diseases (usually affecting both kidneys).

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: These forms usually progress to end-stage kidney failure (_____) over weeks to years (depending on type)
Glomerulonephritis.fact: These forms usually progress to end-stage kidney failure (ESKF) over weeks to years (depending on type).

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: The cause of about 20–_____ of focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis is unknown
Glomerulonephritis.fact: The cause of about 20–30% of focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis is unknown.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: About _____ of cases are due to mutations in the fibronectin (FN1) gene located on chromosome 2 (2q34)
Glomerulonephritis.fact: About 40% of cases are due to mutations in the fibronectin (FN1) gene located on chromosome 2 (2q34).

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Type 2 MPGN, also known as _____, is characterised by an excessive activation of the complement system
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Type 2 MPGN, also called Dense Deposit Disease, is characterised by an excessive activation of the complement system.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: The C3 _____ autoantibody stabilizes C3-convertase, which may lead to an excessive activation of complement
Glomerulonephritis.fact: The C3 Nephritic Factor autoantibody stabilizes C3-convertase, which may lead to an excessive activation of complement.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Type 3 _____, which is caused by immune complex deposition in the subepithelial space
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Type 2 MPGN, also called Dense Deposit Disease, is characterised by an excessive activation of the complement system. Type 2 MPGN is a subgroup of C3 glomerulopathy, a newly proposed diagnosis which also encompasses C3 Glomerulonephritis (C3GN).

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Three main subtypes are recognised: Type 1 is _____ syndrome, an autoimmune disease also affecting the lung
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Three main subtypes are recognised: Type 1 is Goodpasture syndrome, an autoimmune disease also affecting the lung. In Goodpasture syndrome, IgG antibodies directed against the glomerular basement membrane trigger an inflammatory reaction, causing a nephritic syndrome and the coughing up of blood.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: No immune deposits can be seen on staining, however blood tests may be positive for the _____ antibody
Glomerulonephritis.fact: No immune deposits can be seen on staining, however blood tests may be positive for the ANCA antibody.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Formation of crescents is initiated by passage of fibrin into the _____ space as a result of increased permeability of glomerular basement membrane
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Formation of crescents is initiated by passage of fibrin into the Bowman space as a result of increased permeability of glomerular basement membrane. Fibrin stimulates the proliferation of endothelial cells of Bowman capsule, and an influx of monocytes.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Fibrin stimulates the proliferation of endothelial cells of _____ capsule, and an influx of monocytes
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Formation of crescents is initiated by passage of fibrin into the Bowman space as a result of increased permeability of glomerular basement membrane. Fibrin stimulates the proliferation of endothelial cells of Bowman capsule, and an influx of monocytes.

Glomerulonephritis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephritis.question: Rapid growing and fibrosis of crescents compresses the capillary loops and decreases the _____ space, which leads to kidney failure within weeks or months
Glomerulonephritis.fact: Formation of crescents is initiated by passage of fibrin into the Bowman space as a result of increased permeability of glomerular basement membrane. Fibrin stimulates the proliferation of endothelial cells of Bowman capsule, and an influx of monocytes.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: The _____ was Inflammatory disease of the kidney.
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: Glomerulonephrosis is a non-inflammatory disease of the kidney (nephrosis) presenting primarily in the glomerulus (a glomerulopathy) as nephrotic syndrome.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: Primary forms include _____ FSGS, which have no known cause, and Genetic FSGS caused by a recessive genetic mutation
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: Primary forms include Idiopathic FSGS, which have no known cause, and Genetic FSGS caused by a recessive genetic mutation.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: Other forms of secondary glomerulonephrosis can be caused by autoimmune disorders such as HIV, Sjögren's Syndrome, and hepatitis B, and _____, including multiple myeloma
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: Other forms of secondary glomerulonephrosis can be caused by autoimmune disorders such as HIV, Sjögren's Syndrome, and hepatitis B, and some cancers, including multiple myeloma.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: The leakage of water into peripheral structures decreases the total fluid volume in circulation, which will activate the Renin-_____-Aldosterone system
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: The leakage of water into peripheral structures decreases the total fluid volume in circulation, which will activate the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone system. However, water will continue to be lost as edema because glomerulonephrosis will continue to cause proteinuria, and prolonged activation of the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone system will cause blood pressure to remain elevated and cause hypertension.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: In cases involving _____, an electron microscope can be used to visualize changes in podocyte structure
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: In cases involving Minimal Change Disease, an electron microscope can be used to visualize changes in podocyte structure.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: In other forms, such as _____, the progression to kidney disease is very common and individuals will inevitably require kidney transplant
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: In other forms, such as Focal Segmental Sclerosis, the progression to kidney disease is very common and individuals will inevitably require kidney transplant.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: In adults, the opposite is true with _____ being the more common
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: In adults, the opposite is true with Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis being the more common.

Glomerulonephrosis.subject: General Science
Glomerulonephrosis.question: This form is found to be 1.5 times more common in men than women, and some studies suggest that it is found in higher incidences in Blacks than Whites and _____
Glomerulonephrosis.fact: This form is found to be 1.5 times more common in men than women, and some studies suggest that it is found in higher incidences in Blacks than Whites and Hispanics.

Glomerulopathy.subject: General Science
Glomerulopathy.question: Cortical microcysts, which are portrayed by cystic dilatation of _____'s spaces, are its defining feature
Glomerulopathy.fact: Cortical microcysts, which are portrayed by cystic dilatation of Bowman's spaces, are its defining feature.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: The _____ was Functional unit of nephron.
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: The glomerulus (pl.: glomeruli) is a network of small blood vessels (capillaries) called a tuft, located at the beginning of a nephron in the kidney. Each of the two kidneys contains about one million nephrons.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: The glomerulus and its surrounding _____'s capsule constitute a renal corpuscle, the basic filtration unit of the kidney
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: The glomerulus and its surrounding Bowman's capsule constitute a renal corpuscle, the basic filtration unit of the kidney.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: 3): there are gaps between the foot processes through which the filtrate flows into _____'s capsule
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: 3): there are gaps between the foot processes through which the filtrate flows into Bowman's capsule.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: The mesangium contains mainly: _____ mesangial cells
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: The mesangium contains mainly: Intraglomerular mesangial cells.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: These vasa recta run adjacent to the descending and ascending loop of _____ and participate in the maintenance of the medullary countercurrent exchange system
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: These vasa recta run adjacent to the descending and ascending loop of Henle and participate in the maintenance of the medullary countercurrent exchange system.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: This arrangement of two arterioles in series determines the high hydrostatic pressure on glomerular capillaries, which is one of the forces that favor filtration to _____'s capsule
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: This arrangement of two arterioles in series determines the high hydrostatic pressure on glomerular capillaries, which is one of the forces that favor filtration to Bowman's capsule.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: Because large and negatively charged proteins have a low permeability, they cannot filtrate easily to _____'s capsule
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: Because large and negatively charged proteins have a low permeability, they cannot filtrate easily to Bowman's capsule.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: About 175 years later, surgeon and anatomist _____ elucidated in detail the capillary architecture of the glomerulus and the continuity between its surrounding capsule and the proximal tubule
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: About 175 years later, surgeon and anatomist William Bowman elucidated in detail the capillary architecture of the glomerulus and the continuity between its surrounding capsule and the proximal tubule.

Glomerulus (kidney).subject: General Science
Glomerulus (kidney).question: Cortical nephrons near the corticomedullary junction (_____ of all nephrons) are called juxtamedullary nephrons
Glomerulus (kidney).fact: Cortical nephrons near the corticomedullary junction (15% of all nephrons) are called juxtamedullary nephrons.

Glossary of elementary quantum mechanics.subject: General Science
Glossary of elementary quantum mechanics.question: There are five known elementary bosons: the four force carrying gauge bosons γ (photon), g (gluon), Z (Z boson) and W (W boson), as well as the _____ boson
Glossary of elementary quantum mechanics.fact: There are five known elementary bosons: the four force carrying gauge bosons γ (photon), g (gluon), Z (Z boson) and W (W boson), as well as the Higgs boson.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Bathypelagic – the open ocean or pelagic zone that extends from a depth of _____ to 4000 meters below the ocean surface
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Bathypelagic – the open ocean or pelagic zone that extends from a depth of 1000 to 4000 meters below the ocean surface.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: The most successful species worldwide, in terms of biomass, may be the _____ krill, with about five times the total biomass of humans
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: The most successful species worldwide, in terms of biomass, may be the Antarctic krill, with about five times the total biomass of humans.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Buoys can be used as temporary markers, called dans, during _____ seine fishing to mark the anchor position of a net, or when fishing with lobster pots to mark the position of the pots
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Buoys can be used as temporary markers, called dans, during Danish seine fishing to mark the anchor position of a net, or when fishing with lobster pots to mark the position of the pots.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Cephalopods – (from the _____ for "head-feet") animals such as squid and octopus where tentacles converge at the head
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Cephalopods – (from the Greek for "head-feet") animals such as squid and octopus where tentacles converge at the head.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Climate change – variation in the _____'s global climate or in regional climates over time
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Climate change – variation in the Earth's global climate or in regional climates over time. These changes can be caused by natural processes on Earth, external factors including variations in sunlight intensity, and more recently by human activities.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: These changes can be caused by natural processes on _____, external factors including variations in sunlight intensity, and more recently by human activities
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Climate change – variation in the Earth's global climate or in regional climates over time. These changes can be caused by natural processes on Earth, external factors including variations in sunlight intensity, and more recently by human activities.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Coriolis effect – due to the _____'s rotation, freely moving objects on the surface of the Earth veer right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern hemisphere
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Coriolis effect – due to the Earth's rotation, freely moving objects on the surface of the Earth veer right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern hemisphere.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: This effect is called the _____ effect, and works, in particular, on winds and ocean currents
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Coriolis effect – due to the Earth's rotation, freely moving objects on the surface of the Earth veer right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern hemisphere. This effect is called the Coriolis effect, and works, in particular, on winds and ocean currents.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Downwelling – A downward movement (sinking) of surface water caused by onshore _____ transport, converging currents or when a water mass becomes more dense than the surrounding water
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Downwelling – A downward movement (sinking) of surface water caused by onshore Ekman transport, converging currents or when a water mass becomes more dense than the surrounding water.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Warm water pools in the east in _____ño conditions and in the west during La Niña conditions
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: El Niño – large scale, cyclical (generally three to seven years), ocean warming and cooling episodes across the equatorial Pacific. Warm water pools in the east in El Niño conditions and in the west during La Niña conditions.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: It begins around _____ (El Niño means Christ child)
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: It begins around Christmas (El Niño means Christ child).

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: The IUCN has calculated the percentage of endangered species as 40 percent of all organisms based on the sample of species that have been evaluated through to _____
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: The IUCN has calculated the percentage of endangered species as 40 percent of all organisms based on the sample of species that have been evaluated through to 2006.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Fishing fleet – an aggregation of fishing vessels of a particular country, such as the _____ fishing fleet, or using a particular gear, such as purse seine fleet
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Fishing fleet – an aggregation of fishing vessels of a particular country, such as the Russian fishing fleet, or using a particular gear, such as purse seine fleet.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Fry – _____ stage of fish immediately after the larvae stage at an age of less than a week
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Fry – Development stage of fish immediately after the larvae stage at an age of less than a week.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Global warming – the increase in the average temperature of the _____'s near-surface air and oceans in recent decades, as well as the projected continuation of this trend
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Global warming – the increase in the average temperature of the Earth's near-surface air and oceans in recent decades, as well as the projected continuation of this trend.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Highly migratory species – a term which has its origins in the _____ on the Law of the Sea
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Highly migratory species – a term which has its origins in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Bathypelagic – the open ocean or pelagic zone that extends from a depth of 1000 to _____ below the ocean surface
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Bathypelagic – the open ocean or pelagic zone that extends from a depth of 1000 to 4000 meters below the ocean surface.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Continental margins constitute about _____ of the oceanic area
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Continental margins constitute about 28% of the oceanic area.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Extending as far as _____ from the slope, it consists of thick sediments which have cascaded down the slope and accumulated as a pile at the base of the slope
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Extending as far as 500 kilometres from the slope, it consists of thick sediments which have cascaded down the slope and accumulated as a pile at the base of the slope.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Epipelagic – The top layer of the ocean from the surface down to about _____
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Epipelagic – The top layer of the ocean from the surface down to about 200 metres.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Generally a state's EEZ extends to a distance of 200 nautical miles (_____) out from its coast
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Generally a state's EEZ extends to a distance of 200 nautical miles (370 km) out from its coast.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Introduced species – _____ brought into an area where it does not naturally occur, but is able to survive and reproduce there
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Incidental mortality can be contrasted with bycatch, which is a general term for the catch of all fish and non-fish species other than the targeted species. Introduced species – Species brought into an area where it does not naturally occur, but is able to survive and reproduce there.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: IUCN – the _____ for the Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources is the world's main authority on the conservation status of species
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: IUCN – the International Union for the Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources is the world's main authority on the conservation status of species.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: They also list extinctions that have occurred since _____ AD and taxa that are extinct in the wild
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: They also list extinctions that have occurred since 1500 AD and taxa that are extinct in the wild.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: IUCN Red List – the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species (also known as the IUCN Red List or Red Data List), created in _____, is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation sta
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: IUCN Red List – the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species (also called the IUCN Red List or Red Data List), created in 1963, is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Jukung – a traditional fishing boat used in _____
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Jukung – a traditional fishing boat used in Indonesia.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Mesopelagic – ocean depths extending from 200 to _____ metres (650 to 3280 feet) below sea level Migration – a systematic (as opposed to random) movement of individuals in a fish stock from one place
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Mesopelagic – ocean depths extending from 200 to 1000 metres (650 to 3280 feet) below sea level Migration – a systematic (as opposed to random) movement of individuals in a fish stock from one place to another.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Morphometrics – _____ which characterise the form, shape and appearance of an animal or plant
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Morphometrics – Measurements which characterise the form, shape and appearance of an animal or plant.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Ocean currents – _____ currents can be divided into surface and deep ocean currents
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Ocean currents – Oceanic currents can be divided into surface and deep ocean currents.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Surface currents can operate to a depth of _____ and apply to about ten percent of water in the ocean
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Surface currents can operate to a depth of 400 meters and apply to about ten percent of water in the ocean.

Glossary of fishery terms.subject: General Science
Glossary of fishery terms.question: Typical euphotic depths vary from only a few centimetres in highly turbid eutrophic lakes, to around _____ in the open ocean
Glossary of fishery terms.fact: Typical euphotic depths vary from only a few centimetres in highly turbid eutrophic lakes, to around 200 metres in the open ocean.

The Persian intellectual Al-Biruni believed that the force of gravity was not unique to the Earth, and he correctly assumed that other heavenly bodies should exert a gravitational attraction as well. In particular, the Spanish Dominican priest Domingo de Soto wrote in 1551 that bodies in free fall uniformly accelerate. Gravity.fact: Newton's theory of gravity ran counter to a key idea of science, both then and now: forces should not rely on instantaneous action at a distance.  Newton was well aware of this issue and his decision to continue anyway marked a shift in scientific thinking away from philosophically sound but empirically flawed models. The issue was not resolved until Einstein's work on relativity in the 20th century.  === Einstein's general relativity === Eventually, astronomers noticed an eccentricity in the orbit of the planet Mercury which could not be explained by Newton's theory: the perihelion of the orbit was increasing by about 42. 98 arcseconds per century. Gravity.fact: === Action principles === A third completely different way to derive a model of gravity is based on action principles.  This formulation represents the effects of gravity on a system in a mathematically abstract way.  The state of the system, for example the position and velocity of every particle, is expressed as a single mathematical entity.  Each state has an associated energy property called the Lagrangian; the physically allowed changes to the state of the system minimize the value of this property.  The path of the state is not a path in physical space, but rather in a high-dimensional state space: each point along the path corresponds to a different position and or velocity collectively for all particles in the system.  This formulation does not express the forces or fields of the individual particles.  Modern theories of physics rely on these action principles

Harmonic analysis.fact: Harmonic analysis is an area of mathematical analysis that emerged from the study of harmonic functions, and especially their boundary behavior. Harmonic analysis.fact: Basic examples include Fourier series and the Fourier transform, while modern harmonic analysis also studies maximal functions, singular integrals, oscillatory integrals, Fourier multipliers, Littlewood–Paley theory, and spectral decompositions. Harmonic analysis overlaps substantially with Fourier analysis, real analysis, functional analysis, partial differential equations, potential theory, ergodic theory, representation theory, and number theory.

Heart.fact: The cardiac muscle pattern is elegant and complex, as the muscle cells swirl and spiral around the chambers of the heart, with the outer muscles forming a figure 8 pattern around the atria and around the bases of the great vessels and the inner muscles, forming a figure 8 around the two ventricles and proceeding toward the apex.  This complex swirling pattern allows the heart to pump blood more effectively.  There are two types of cells in cardiac muscle: muscle cells which have the ability to contract easily, and pacemaker cells of the conducting system.  The muscle cells make up the bulk (99%) of cells in the atria and ventricles.  These contractile cells are connected by intercalated discs which allow a rapid response to impulses of action potential from the pacemaker cells.  The intercalated discs allow the cells to act as a syncytium and enable the contractions that pump blood through the heart and into the major arteries.  The pacemaker cells make up 1% of cells and form the conduction system of the heart

The intercalated discs allow the cells to act as a syncytium and enable the contractions that pump blood through the heart and into the major arteries.  The pacemaker cells make up 1% of cells and form the conduction system of the heart.  They are generally much smaller than the contractile cells and have few myofibrils which gives them limited contractibility.  Their function is similar in many respects to neurons.  Cardiac muscle tissue has autorhythmicity, the unique ability to initiate a cardiac action potential at a fixed rate—spreading the impulse rapidly from cell to cell to trigger the contraction of the entire heart

Heart.fact: ==== Electrocardiogram ==== Using surface electrodes on the body, it is possible to record the electrical activity of the heart.  This tracing of the electrical signal is the electrocardiogram (ECG) or (EKG).  An ECG is a bedside test and involves the placement of ten leads on the body.  This produces a "12 lead" ECG (three extra leads are calculated mathematically, and one lead is electrically ground, or earthed). These ideas went unchallenged for almost a thousand years.  === Pre-modern === The earliest descriptions of the coronary and pulmonary circulation systems can be found in the Commentary on Anatomy in Avicenna's Canon, published in 1242 by Ibn al-Nafis. Hydroelectricity.subject: General Science
Hydroelectricity.question: The _____ and LHP categories are further subdivided into many subcategories that are not mutually exclusive
Hydroelectricity.fact: == Sizes, types and capacities of hydroelectric facilities == The classification of hydropower plants starts with two top-level categories: small hydropower plants (SHP) and large hydropower plants (LHP).  The classification of a plant as an SHP or LHP is primarily based on its nameplate capacity, the threshold varies by the country, but in any case a plant with the capacity of 50 MW or more is considered an LHP.  As an example, for China, SHP power is below 25 MW, for India – below 15 MW, most of Europe – below 10 MW.  The SHP and LHP categories are further subdivided into many subcategories that are not mutually exclusive.  For example, a low-head hydro power plant with hydrostatic head of few meters to few tens of meters can be classified either as an SHP or an LHP.  The other distinction between SHP and LHP is the degree of the water flow regulation: a typical SHP primarily uses the natural water discharge with very little regulation in comparison to an LHP.  Therefore, the term SHP is frequently used as a synonym for the run-of-the-river power plant

Hydroelectricity.subject: General Science
Hydroelectricity.question: The turbines also will kill large portions of the fauna passing through, for instance _____ of the eel passing a turbine will perish immediately
Hydroelectricity.fact: Hydroelectric projects can be disruptive to surrounding aquatic ecosystems both upstream and downstream of the plant site.  Generation of hydroelectric power changes the downstream river environment.  Water exiting a turbine usually contains very little suspended sediment, which can lead to scouring of river beds and loss of riverbanks.  The turbines also will kill large portions of the fauna passing through, for instance 70% of the eel passing a turbine will perish immediately.  Since turbine gates are often opened intermittently, rapid or even daily fluctuations in river flow are observed.  ==== Drought and water loss by evaporation ==== Drought and seasonal changes in rainfall can severely limit hydropower.  Water may also be lost by evaporation

Hydroelectricity.fact: Lower river flows will reduce the amount of live storage in a reservoir therefore reducing the amount of water that can be used for hydroelectricity. One study from the Colorado River in the United States suggest that modest climate changes, such as an increase in temperature in 2 degree Celsius resulting in a 10% decline in precipitation, might reduce river run-off by up to 40%.  Brazil in particular is vulnerable due to its heavy reliance on hydroelectricity, as increasing temperatures, lower water flow and alterations in the rainfall regime, could reduce total energy production by 7% annually by the end of the century.  ==== Methane emissions (from reservoirs) ==== Lower positive impacts are found in the tropical regions. Hydroelectricity.subject: General Science
Hydroelectricity.question: Due to high population and availability of cheap labour, countries in the _____, such as India and China have the lowest overall hydropower investment costs
Hydroelectricity.fact: == Economics == The development of hydropower projects typically includes high costs of setting up due to requirement of intense labour and expense on plant and machinery.  Conducting analysis of the impact of hydropower generation and compensating for any negative impacts also adds up to the final cost.  Though total greenfield hydropower investment typically costs between USD 1,200/Kw and USD 4,500/Kw, the range can be much wider for large-scale hydropower plants, ranging from 1,000/Kw to 10,000/Kw, according to IEA report 2021 on hydropower generation.  Due to high population and availability of cheap labour, countries in the Asia Pacific, such as India and China have the lowest overall hydropower investment costs.  On the other hand, countries in Europe and North America have the highest hydropower investment costs due to expensive labour.  In Africa, the major issue is the backward technology and infrastructure which is not compatible for hydro-power generation.  Capital costs usually make-up 80-90% of hydropower’s levelised cost of energy (LCOE)

Hydroelectricity.subject: General Science

Hydroelectricity.fact: Due to high population and availability of cheap labour, countries in the Asia Pacific, such as India and China have the lowest overall hydropower investment costs.  On the other hand, countries in Europe and North America have the highest hydropower investment costs due to expensive labour.  In Africa, the major issue is the backward technology and infrastructure which is not compatible for hydro-power generation.  Capital costs usually make-up 80-90% of hydropower’s levelised cost of energy (LCOE).  Operations and maintenance (O&M) account for the remainder, which on average amounts to about 2% of the initial investment cost.  Project development costs and expected returns on investment, expressed as the weighted average cost of capital is a major factor.  == See also == == References == == Sources == Kuriqi, Alban; Jurasz, Jakub (2022)

Hypogonadism.subject: General Science
Hypogonadism.question: The _____ was Diminished activity of the gonads.

Hypogonadism, commonly referred to by the symptom "low testosterone" or "low T", can also decrease other hormones secreted by the gonads including progesterone, DHEA, anti-Müllerian hormone, activin, and inhibin.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.question: The _____ was Diminished gonad activity due to dysfunction of the hypothalamus or pituitary gland.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.fact: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH), is a disorder where the pituitary gland fails to produce the required levels of the hormones (LH and/or FSH) which are needed to stimulate the gonads (testicles or ovaries) to function normally.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.fact: FSH acts on Sertoli cells in the male and follicular cells in the female.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.subject: General Science
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.question: The production of sex steroids forms a negative feedback loop acting on both the anterior pituitary and hypothalamus causing a pulsatile secretion of _____
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.fact: The production of sex steroids forms a negative feedback loop acting on both the anterior pituitary and hypothalamus causing a pulsatile secretion of GnRH. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.subject: General Science

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.fact: CHH itself can be further divided into 2 subtypes depending on the condition of the olfactory system, anosmic HH (Kallman syndrome) and normosmic HH.

Jiugongdao.fact: Jiugongdao (九宫道 "Way of the Nine Palaces") is a Chinese folk religious sect centered in the Wutai County of the province of Shanxi. Flourishing in the Qing dynasty, but rooted in earlier times, the Jiugongdao developed greatly on Mount Wutai thanks to the efforts of Li Xiangshan, also called Puji, his name as a Buddhist monk who was close to the Manchu court.
